ai.definition: Satellite technologies involve the deployment of artificial satellites in space to provide communication services such as internet access, data transmission, and other IoT applications. Low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations are particularly noted for their potential to offer high-speed internet and global connectivity.
ai.howItWorks: LEO satellites orbit at altitudes between 160 km and 2,000 km above Earth's surface. They communicate with ground stations and other satellites to relay data. Miniaturized electronics and advanced materials enable these satellites to be compact yet highly functional, allowing for large constellations that can cover vast areas.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing the challenges of providing internet access in remote or underserved regions where traditional infrastructure is unavailable or uneconomical.
ai.manufacturing: Satellites are manufactured using advanced composite materials and miniaturized electronics. The build process involves precise assembly, rigorous testing, and integration with launch vehicles.
ai.buildProcess: The satellite design includes the development of electronic components, mechanical structures, and communication systems. These are then assembled into a functional unit that can withstand the rigors of space travel and operation.
ai.costDrivers: High initial investment in R&D, manufacturing costs, and launch expenses. Ongoing operational costs include maintenance, fuel for orbit adjustments, and ground station infrastructure.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is currently being deployed commercially with significant growth expected as more companies enter the market and expand their services.
ai.regulation: Regulations vary by country but generally involve licensing for launch, operation, and spectrum use. International agreements also govern space debris management and satellite collision avoidance.
ai.risks: Technical risks include system failures, orbital debris, and cybersecurity threats. Economic risks stem from high initial costs and potential oversaturation of the market.
ai.profitability: Profitability is variable depending on the business model, scale of operations, and competition in the market. Successful companies can achieve significant returns through subscription services and data sales.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may include further miniaturization of components, improved solar panel efficiency for power generation, and advanced AI systems for autonomous satellite operation.

glossary.def: Low-Earth orbit, referring to satellites that operate between 160 km and 2,000 km above Earth's surface.
A group of satellites working together in a coordinated manner to provide continuous coverage and services.
A facility on the ground used for receiving and transmitting data between satellites and users.

subsystems.name: Spacecraft bus
subsystems.role: the body that holds everything together and keeps it pointing.

subsystems.name: Communications payload
subsystems.role: forms and steers radio beams to and from the ground.

subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: generates and stores electricity through sun and eclipse.

subsystems.name: Propulsion
subsystems.role: raises the satellite into its working orbit and keeps the constellation spaced.

subsystems.name: Ground segment
subsystems.role: connects the constellation to the internet.

subsystems.name: User terminal
subsystems.role: the flat antenna and modem on a roof, ship or aircraft.

buildSteps.title: Design for mass production
buildSteps.detail: Instead of one-off spacecraft, satellites are redesigned as flat, stackable units that fit many per rocket fairing.

buildSteps.title: Build the bus on a line
buildSteps.detail: Structure, avionics, batteries and solar arrays are assembled at stations like a vehicle factory, with automated testing between steps.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the payload
buildSteps.detail: Phased-array panels and the digital processor are fitted, then the satellite is characterised in an anechoic chamber to map its beams.

buildSteps.title: Environmental test
buildSteps.detail: Each unit is shaken on a vibration table and cycled in a thermal-vacuum chamber to survive launch and the space environment.

buildSteps.title: Launch and deploy
buildSteps.detail: Satellites ride a dispenser on a rocket; once in a low parking orbit they separate and unfurl their solar arrays.

buildSteps.title: Raise orbit and phase
buildSteps.detail: Electric thrusters slowly lift each satellite to its working altitude and slot it into the correct orbital plane.

buildSteps.title: Build the ground network
buildSteps.detail: Gateway stations are installed in countries with landing rights, connected by fibre to internet exchange points.

buildSteps.title: Produce terminals and activate users
buildSteps.detail: Terminals are manufactured at scale, shipped, self-aligned by the customer's app, and provisioned on the network.

buildSteps.title: Operate and deorbit
buildSteps.detail: The operator tracks conjunction warnings, manoeuvres to avoid collisions, and retires satellites into a controlled atmospheric burn-up.

prerequisites.why: constellations need hundreds to thousands of satellites launched at a price per kilogram that only reuse has delivered.
mechanically moving dishes cannot track fast-moving LEO satellites or be mass-produced cheaply.
optical crosslinks let satellites route traffic in space, cutting the number of ground stations needed.
operators must obtain national licences and coordinate frequencies internationally before serving customers.
building several satellites per day, rather than per year, is what makes the economics work.

pathway.milestone: thousands of LEO satellites delivering broadband to homes, ships and aircraft, with latency of tens of milliseconds
pathway.unlocks: connectivity in remote and rural areas beyond the reach of fibre.

pathway.milestone: direct-to-phone service, where an ordinary mobile handset connects to a satellite with no extra dish
pathway.unlocks: coverage in dead zones and during disasters.

pathway.milestone: laser-meshed constellations that route traffic between satellites instead of via ground gateways
pathway.unlocks: service over oceans and in countries that grant no landing rights.

pathway.milestone: routine end-of-life deorbit and active debris management built into every constellation
pathway.unlocks: a sustainable low-Earth orbit environment for the next generation of operators.
